thread:
Anita: noticed a class of failures in intake today: models with nonstandard tokenizers pass basic lint but later fail reranker evals due to subtle normalization differences. Example: unicode normalization NFKC vs NFC causing different token splits.

Ravi: ugh. Those can be subtle. We should capture a tokenizer_fingerprint at ingest (normalizer config, vocab hash, model declared vocab size) and use it in routing + later debugging.

Drew: agree. Thinking of a lightweight tokenizer-probe that runs 120 random eval samples and computes: unknown_rate, roundtrip_idempotence, max_id, median_token_len, normalizer_diff_count. If any metric trips, move to deepbench.

Anita: requirements: probe must be cheap (<2s median added latency) and safe for byte-level models. So models can declare tokenizer_kind: {byte, sentencepiece, bpe, hybrid}. Byte models skip unknown_rate check.

ingest-bot: enqueue 1781239999 | tokenizer-probe(samples=120) :gear:

Ravi: propose fingerprint format = sha256 of (tokenizer.json + normalizer config + vocab file) and persist as hex string in registry. Also store tokenizer_kind and declared_vocab_size as metadata strings.

Drew: routing changes: intake-router should consult probe outcome with three states: PASS, WARN, FAIL. PASS -> fastpath. WARN -> fastpath but attach warning and schedule deepbench in background. FAIL -> block and create deepbench ticket with probe output.

Anita: for WARN thresholds: unknown_rate < 0.05 and roundtrip_idempotence >= 0.9. For FAIL: unknown_rate >= 0.1 or any id_overflow > 0 or normalizer_diff_count > 10. Adjust later per family.

Ravi: telemetry: emit tokenizer_probe.latency_ms, tokenizer_probe.unknown_rate, tokenizer_probe.roundtrip, tokenizer_probe.max_id, tokenizer_probe.result_state. Good for dashboards.

Drew: implement details: probe runs in async worker pool. Intake will wait synchronously up to 3s for probe result. If no result within timeout, assume WARN and continue fastpath but mark 'probe_pending'.

Anita: tests: add unit tests for sentencepiece with NFKC vs NFC normalization, and for a toy byte-level tokenizer to ensure we don't false-positive. Also add integration test where probe triggers FAIL and router creates deepbench ticket.

Ravi: I'll add the registry schema change (tokenizer_fingerprint, tokenizer_kind, declared_vocab_size) and migration plan to backfill existing models with a fingerprint job.

Drew: I'll add the probe implementation and a small CLI for local testing:

```
# local dev
python infra/tokenizer_probe.py --model-dir ./model --samples 120 --out ./probe_out.json
cat ./probe_out.json
```

Anita: owners: Drew -> probe impl + tests; Ravi -> registry + telemetry + router wiring; I'll draft a short RFC to lock thresholds and walk through edge cases (byte-level, vocab overlays).

Drew: one more: persist the short human-readable probe summary (one-line) to model metadata to surface in the console. Makes debugging painless for SRE/customer.

Anita: agreed. Ok let's land small PRs: probe first, registry second, router third. We keep the async timeout conservative (3s) and put heavy work on deepbench. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
